title: STATUS OF NATIONAL RIVERS INTERLINKING PROGRAMME
body_text:
Government of India formulated the National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Inter-Basin Water Transfer and 30 Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) Projects were identified under NPP (16 link projects under the Peninsular component and 14 link projects under the Himalayan component). National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has been entrusted with the work of ILR. The present status of all 30 ILR projects is at Annexure .
The Ken-Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is the only priority link project under the NPP that has entered the implementation stage. The project, with an estimated cost of ₹44,605 crore, is envisaged to provide irrigation to about 11.88 lakh hectares, drinking water supply to about 62 lakh people, 103 MW of hydropower and 27 MW of solar power.
In addition, the Polavaram Irrigation Project (PIP), which incorporates the Godavari (Polavaram)–Krishna (Vijayawada) link, stands classified as a National Project and is executed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh and Polavaram Project Authority (PPA). The project envisages irrigation to about 7.2 lakh acres and stabilization of 23.5 lakh acres in the Godavari and Krishna delta systems, diversion of 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna basin, drinking and industrial water supply including to Visakhapatnam, domestic water supply to about 28.5 lakh population in 611 villages, and hydropower generation of 960 MW. The Polavaram Irrigation Project has received cumulative Central Assistance of ₹20,658 crore.
An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) forms part of the preparation of Feasibility Reports (FRs) and Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for every Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) project, with assessment of environmental and socio‑economic impacts. For the Ken–Betwa Link Project, a comprehensive EIA has been completed along with an Integrated Landscape Management Plan (ILMP), which outlines measures relating to catchment‑area treatment, landscape‑level ecological management, biodiversity conservation, command‑area development and long‑term monitoring of environmental parameters. For all ILR projects, including the Ken–Betwa Link Project, Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation & Resettlement (R&R) components stand included in the sanctioned project structure, and project execution conforms to applicable environmental, forest‑clearance and R&R provisions.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti informed the Rajya Sabha about the status of India's 30 identified Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) projects under the National Perspective Plan (16 Peninsular and 14 Himalayan links), managed by the National Water Development Agency. The Ken-Betwa Link Project, costing ₹44,605 crore, is the only priority link project under implementation, expected to irrigate 11.88 lakh hectares and supply drinking water to 62 lakh people. The Polavaram Irrigation Project, a National Project executed by Andhra Pradesh, has received ₹20,658 crore in central assistance and incorporates the Godavari-Krishna link. Most other projects remain at feasibility report, DPR, or pre-feasibility stages, with some (like Damanganga-Pinjal, Par-Tapi-Narmada, and Kosi-Mechi) dropped from priority status.
enrichment.context:
The National Perspective Plan for river interlinking was conceived in 1980 to address India's uneven water distribution by transferring surplus water from water-rich basins (like the Ganga-Brahmaputra) to water-deficit regions (like peninsular India), aiming to enhance irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydropower generation. The programme has faced decades of delays due to inter-state water disputes, environmental concerns, high costs, and questions about the surplus/deficit water assessments underlying the plan. The Ken-Betwa Link Project, connecting Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, became the first project to move into implementation after years of negotiation, involving significant environmental trade-offs including submergence of parts of the Panna Tiger Reserve, which necessitated the Integrated Landscape Management Plan for biodiversity conservation.

The Polavaram project on the Godavari river in Andhra Pradesh has been a politically sensitive National Project since 2014, tied to Andhra Pradesh's post-bifurcation development commitments. River interlinking also raises federal and international dimensions, as seen with the Kosi-Mechi project's cross-border complications with Nepal, highlighting how water-sharing negotiations extend beyond domestic politics into diplomatic terrain. This periodic parliamentary reporting on project status reflects ongoing scrutiny of the programme's slow pace and its evolving environmental and social safeguard requirements.

prelims_questions.question: The Ken-Betwa Link Project, the first river interlinking project to enter implementation, connects rivers flowing through which two states?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the PIB release, the Ken-Betwa link project benefits Uttar Pradesh (UP) and Madhya Pradesh (MP), and is the only priority link project under the NPP that has entered the implementation stage.

prelims_questions.question: Under the National Perspective Plan for Interlinking of Rivers, the 30 identified projects are classified into which two components?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that 30 ILR projects were identified under NPP, comprising 16 link projects under the Peninsular component and 14 link projects under the Himalayan component.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives and challenges associated with India's National Perspective Plan for Interlinking of Rivers. Evaluate the progress and environmental concerns related to the Ken-Betwa Link Project.

River water disputes often have inter-state and international dimensions. Discuss this in the context of the dropped Kosi-Mechi inter-state link project and its implications for cooperative federalism and river basin management in India.
